appView.description: Browse every image you generated, with the model, quality and size it was made with.
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
diag.hint.dns: The host name could not be resolved. Check the endpoint domain, your proxy, or the system DNS — a proxy set to "system proxy" mode sometimes keeps DNS local and breaks it.
diag.hint.envProxy: This request went out directly, but your system environment defines {proxy}. Set it in this tool's settings (Network Proxy) so the request actually uses it.
diag.hint.invalidProxy: The proxy address was rejected as invalid. It should look like http://127.0.0.1:7890 — a scheme plus host and port.
diag.hint.noProxy: No proxy is configured. If you need one to reach the API, set it in this tool's settings (Network Proxy).
diag.hint.refused: The connection was actively refused: nothing is listening on that port. Start your proxy client, or fix the proxy address/port.
diag.hint.reset: The connection was reset mid-transfer. Usually a proxy or firewall dropping the request; try again, and if it repeats check the proxy rules for this domain.
diag.hint.timeout: The connection timed out. The proxy is probably not running, or the network cannot reach it — verify the proxy port, or switch the proxy to a working node.
diag.hint.tls: TLS verification failed, which usually means something intercepted the connection (corporate proxy, VPN, antivirus). Point the proxy setting at your real HTTP proxy instead of a TLS-intercepting one.
diag.title: Failed at "{stage}" after {ms} ms.
dialog.apiKey.desc: Paste your OpenAI API key. It is stored locally and only sent to the API endpoint used by Image Tool — never shown in chat.
dialog.baseUrl.desc: OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. a proxy/relay endpoint. Leave empty to use the official {default}.
dialog.invalidUrl.message: "{value}" is not a valid http(s) URL. The base URL was not changed.
dialog.invalidUrl.title: Invalid URL
dialog.proxy.desc: Used for every request to the image API. Leave empty to follow the system environment ({env}). Example: http://127.0.0.1:7890
error.gifMask: GIF output does not support masks or markup — generate a plain animation, or switch to png to edit a specific area.
error.inputFormat: Reference images must be png, jpeg or webp. "{file}" is not one of those — convert it first (or, for an image the tool generated, ask for that format instead).
error.noKey: OpenAI API key is not configured. Ask the user to open the Image Tool entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu → "OpenAI API Key" to enter it, then retry.
error.svgEdit: output_format "svg" cannot be combined with reference_image_paths — the API generates SVG only from a prompt and does not edit existing images into SVG. Ask for png/webp for an edit, or drop the reference images.
error.svgSingle: output_format "svg" generates exactly one file, so n must be 1.
error.tooManyReferences: Too many reference images: the API accepts at most {max} per request.

probe.auth.detail: The request arrived at {baseUrl} — the proxy, DNS and TLS are fine. The API returned {status}, so the key itself was rejected: check it in this same settings menu, and for GPT Image models make sure your OpenAI organization is verified.
probe.failed.detail: Could not reach the image API at all. Details below tell you which step failed and which proxy was used.
probe.noKey.detail: Add an OpenAI API Key in this settings menu first, then test again.
probe.ok.detail: The endpoint {baseUrl} answered in {ms} ms and accepted the key. Proxy, DNS and TLS are all working — image generation should go through.
result.fromPartial: The endpoint streamed previews but no final image, so the last preview was saved — it may be lower resolution than requested.
systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths, up to 16 of them, for editing or compositing several references); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area, or markup_path with a transparent PNG of the user's marks laid over the first reference to guide the edit (mask and markup cannot be combined). COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.6-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.6-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. complexity (low/medium/high) buys planning separately from rendering quality and also costs time, so leave it unset unless the composition is genuinely demanding. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the gallery (left sidebar App View, or the tool panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. On older Finch builds, gallery edits arrive as image annotations containing the marked preview and complete request. Current Finch carries the same request through reference syntax instead: the reference names the marked preview — the picture carrying the requested changes — and lists each comment with its percentage position, while the user's own wording stays plain message text. Pass the referenced picture's path in reference_image_paths, treat that marked picture as the source to change, and follow every comment without reproducing the red markup or numbered pins in the result. When the user instead writes their own request, follow that text and treat the attached image as the source. From the sidebar App View — which has no input box — the same edit arrives as a chat message with two images: the first is the ORIGINAL to edit and the second is the marked preview. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to open the Image Tool entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in. That settings menu also holds the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com. The Image Tool button in the Composer toolbar sets the everyday generation defaults instead: default model, default quality and default size (a single image_gen_create call can still override model/quality/size, or base_url for a one-off endpoint). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.
tool.description:
Generate an image with OpenAI's GPT Image API, or edit/remix one using reference images and an optional mask.
- Text-to-image: pass only "prompt".
- Image-to-image (reference-guided generation/editing): also pass "reference_image_paths" with local absolute image file paths (several are allowed, up to 16, for editing or compositing references); add "mask_path" to restrict the edit to a masked area, or "markup_path" to hand over a transparent PNG of the user's marks over the first reference (GPT Image 2.5/2.6; mask and markup cannot be combined).
- size takes "auto" or WIDTHxHEIGHT: 1024x1024 (square), 1536x1024 (landscape), 1024x1536 (portrait), 2048x2048, 2048x1152, 2560x1440, 3840x2160. Custom sizes need multiples of 16, an aspect ratio within 3:1, edges ≤3840px.
- quality: low (fast drafts) → medium → high → xhigh → max. Unless the user asks for better, stay on the cheap defaults (gpt-image-2.6-flare + low + 1024x1024); higher quality and larger sizes cost more and take longer. complexity low/medium/high is planning effort, separate from quality — omit it unless asked.
- background "transparent" (with output_format png/webp) gives a cut-out image. output_format is png/jpeg/webp by default, and image 2.6 also makes gif and svg: gif animates 2-16 frames (frame_count, frame_duration_ms) and cannot be masked, streamed or compressed; svg is vector output authored from the prompt only, so it cannot be combined with reference images and needs n=1 (svg_model / svg_effort pick the author model when the account has SVG model selection).
- For a slow single render, partial_images 1-3 streams low-resolution previews so progress stays visible.
Generated images are saved to local files and collected in the gallery (left sidebar App View, or the tool panel in a session), where the user can preview images, draw lines and add multiple numbered comments. Gallery edits arrive as image annotations on older Finch, or through reference syntax on current Finch (the reference names the marked picture to change and lists the numbered comments; the user's wording stays plain text). Both carry every comment, its position and the picture to work from: pass the referenced image's path in reference_image_paths, follow all comments, and never reproduce the annotation marks in the output. Use wechat_send or Session attach afterward to show/share the images — do not try to re-download or re-encode them yourself.
Requests go to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in this mini tool's settings menu in Toolcase (default api.openai.com); pass base_url to override it for a single call only, and set that menu's "Network Proxy" when the machine reaches the internet through a local proxy (leave it empty to follow HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY). The same menu has "Test Connection", which lists models instead of generating anything.
A failed call returns the API error code plus a remediation hint — change the prompt, size or inputs as instructed rather than retrying unchanged. A connection failure instead reports the failing stage, the proxy in use and the full cause chain: relay that to the user and send them to "Network Proxy" / "Test Connection" rather than retrying the image request.

warn.compressionDropped: output_compression applies to jpeg/webp only and was ignored for {format}.
warn.framesClamped: frame_count {requested} is outside 2-16 and was clamped to {used}.
warn.streamUnsupported: This endpoint does not stream previews for {format} output, so partial_images was ignored.
warn.svgEffortNeedsModel: svg_effort needs svg_model — without an author model the effort is ignored.
warn.svgIgnored: svg_model only applies to SVG output and was ignored.
warn.transparentFormat: A transparent background is only available for png and webp, so the format was changed from {format} to png.
